title: QuerySets and the SQL behind them

steps.label: Lazy
steps.note: Building a QuerySet runs no SQL: zero queries. .query only shows the SQL Django would send (without quoting the values).

steps.label: filter + order_by
steps.note: Iterating (here: list()) runs it. Field lookups like year__lt become WHERE clauses; order_by becomes ORDER BY.
sql: SELECT "shop_book"."id", "shop_book"."title", "shop_book"."author_id", "shop_book"."year", "shop_book"."copies" FROM "shop_book" WHERE "shop_book"."year" < 1900 ORDER BY "shop_book"."year" DESC

steps.label: get
steps.note: get() returns exactly one object. With no match it raises DoesNotExist; with two, MultipleObjectsReturned.

steps.label: Q objects (OR)
steps.note: Keyword arguments are ANDed. For OR (or NOT, with ~Q) combine Q objects.

steps.label: Across a relation
steps.note: author__name follows the foreign key: Django writes the JOIN. values_list returns plain values instead of model objects.
sql: SELECT "shop_book"."title" AS "title" FROM "shop_book" INNER JOIN "shop_author" ON ("shop_book"."author_id" = "shop_author"."id") WHERE "shop_author"."name" = 'Jane Austen'

steps.label: annotate
steps.note: annotate adds a computed column per row: here COUNT with GROUP BY, one row per author.
sql: SELECT "shop_author"."name" AS "name", COUNT("shop_book"."id") AS "n" FROM "shop_author" LEFT OUTER JOIN "shop_book" ON ("shop_author"."id" = "shop_book"."author_id") GROUP BY "shop_author"."id", 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC

steps.label: aggregate
steps.note: aggregate summarises the whole QuerySet into one dict.
sql: SELECT AVG("shop_book"."year") AS "avg_year", COUNT("shop_book"."id") AS "total" FROM "shop_book"

steps.label: update with F()
steps.note: One UPDATE for every matching row, and F() makes the database do the arithmetic: no read-modify-write race. Returns the number of rows changed.

steps.label: exists
steps.note: exists() asks only 'is there at least one?' (LIMIT 1), far cheaper than len() or count() when that's all you need.

steps.label: Slicing
steps.note: Slicing a QuerySet becomes LIMIT/OFFSET in SQL, not a Python slice of every row.
sql: SELECT "shop_book"."id", "shop_book"."title", "shop_book"."author_id", "shop_book"."year", "shop_book"."copies" FROM "shop_book" ORDER BY "shop_book"."title" ASC LIMIT 2
